variant.recon_evidence: The media proxy fetches the supplied image_url server-side and echoes the raw upstream body in the 502 error page when the fetch fails; responses to external CDNs confirm outbound fetches are unrestricted and the app runs on EC2.

variant.expected_success_signal: Directory listing containing ami-id, hostname, iam, etc. echoed in the proxy error body.

variant.recon_evidence: Recon shows a WAF rule returning 403 specifically for requests whose callback value contains the literal dotted string 169.254.169.254, while the metadata path /latest/meta-data/ alone passes unblocked.

variant.expected_success_signal: Metadata directory listing returned instead of the expected 403 WAF block.
variant.reasoning: 2852039166 is the 32-bit integer form of 169.254.169.254, so the socket layer resolves it to the metadata address while the WAF's dotted-quad regex never matches, which is the documented bypass for the observed behaviour.

variant.recon_evidence: The webhook test feature issues an outbound HTTP request to webhook_url and returns the first 2 KB of the response; every IPv4 textual form of 169.254.169.254 (dotted, decimal, octal) is blocked by the egress filter.

variant.expected_success_signal: Metadata directory listing appearing in the returned webhook response snippet.
variant.reasoning: ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe is the IPv6-mapped form of 169.254.169.254, so a stack that accepts IPv6 literals translates it back to the link-local IPv4 metadata address and slips past an IPv4-only egress filter.

variant.recon_evidence: The thumbnail route takes the source URL directly from the path segment (after /cdn/thumbnail/) and fetches it server-side; the segpath is not normalised and the app runs on EC2.

variant.recon_evidence: The preview endpoint reads a URL from the X-Resource-Location request header and fetches it to render a link preview; IPv4 textual forms of the metadata address are rejected, but header values are not run through the same egress validation as query parameters.

variant.expected_success_signal: Metadata directory listing rendered into the link preview response.
variant.reasoning: The header value feeds the same server-side fetch, and using the IPv6-mapped encoding of 169.254.169.254 relies on the header path not sharing the IPv4-focused egress filter, which makes the outcome somewhat speculative.

variant.recon_evidence: Container environment exposes AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI=/v2/credentials/xxxx and ECS task metadata endpoint reachable from the pod network.

variant.recon_evidence: Application runs as an ECS task behind Fargate; IMDSv2 hop limit blocks 169.254.169.254 but the container credential endpoint answers on the link-local address.
variant.planner_rationale: The proxy takes the destination as a form field, so post the ECS credential URL as the target body parameter.

variant.recon_evidence: Workload deployed on GCP; compute metadata v1 requires the Metadata-Flavor: Google header while the v1beta1 endpoint returns 403, and the fetcher only forwards user-controlled query parameters.
variant.planner_rationale: Use gopher to emit a raw HTTP request that includes the mandatory Metadata-Flavor header the fetcher cannot set.
variant.expected_success_signal: Instance ssh-keys attribute returned in the preview body with Metadata-Flavor satisfied in the raw request
variant.reasoning: gopher permits arbitrary raw TCP bytes, so the SSRF can carry the exact HTTP request including Metadata-Flavor: Google that plain URL fetching cannot supply, which is precisely the header gate observed during recon.

variant.recon_evidence: Header-based fetch endpoint on a GCP instance where the renderer rejects direct metadata.google.internal hosts but forwards the X-Source-Url header verbatim to its HTTP client.
variant.planner_rationale: Supply the crafted gopher request through the header the renderer copies into its outbound request.
variant.expected_success_signal: SSH keys from the instance attributes appear in the rendered output
variant.reasoning: The header-controlled fetcher still cannot attach Metadata-Flavor to an http URL, so gopher's raw request bytes are required; confidence is slightly lower because it depends on the client honouring an arbitrary scheme supplied via a header.

variant.recon_evidence: Cluster fingerprints point to Hetzner Cloud (floating IP and hcloud agent banners); AWS and GCP metadata paths returned no content while the link-local address responded.
variant.planner_rationale: Probe the vendor-specific Hetzner metadata route to enumerate the instance from the internal network position.
variant.expected_success_signal: JSON containing hostname, instance-id, region and public IPv4/IPv6 addresses
variant.reasoning: Hetzner exposes its inventory at /hetzner/v1/metadata on the link-local address, matching the observed vendor fingerprints, so this path yields the instance metadata the standard AWS-style listing does not.

variant.recon_evidence: Render worker accepts an arbitrary source_url and always terminates after a fixed 5s timeout; no scheme denylist observed when testing http/https/data, and outbound connect errors surface as a generic 'unsupported source' string rather than a validation error.
variant.planner_rationale: sftp forces an SSH handshake to an external host, giving us a clean OOB proof that the renderer dials arbitrary schemes from inside the VPC.
variant.expected_success_signal: Full SSH-2.0 identification string from the renderer's sftp client logged on our listener, paired with the render job failing at the 5s timeout
variant.reasoning: Because the renderer appears to hand the string straight to a URL-aware fetch library rather than validating the scheme, sftp survives and triggers a real SSH banner exchange. The resulting client version string fingerprints the internal egress stack and confirms the injection point is the JSON body field.

variant.recon_evidence: Responses are delivered by a dispatcher that logs a 'validated url' line at enqueue time and a separate 'resolved host' line at send time; a replay of the same hostname produced two different A records in the dispatcher log.
variant.planner_rationale: Double resolution gives us TOCTOU: the validator sees the public address while the dispatcher connects to the rebound169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint.
variant.expected_success_signal: Dispatcher 'resolved host' line showing 169.254.169.254 and a delivery attempt carrying the instance metadata document back through the webhook target
variant.reasoning: The two distinct A records observed across enqueue and send confirm a genuine resolve-then-connect gap, and the rotating-answer hostname lets the first lookup pass validation while the second lands on the link-local metadata IP. The payload fits because it needs only the hostname itself, with no scheme or path that a filter would choke on.

variant.recon_evidence: The preview endpoint ignores the src query argument and instead renders whatever URL is stored in the widget_src cookie; setting the cookie to http://127.0.0.1:6379/ produced a connection-refused page rendered in the widget iframe, proving server-side fetches honour cookie-supplied URLs.
variant.planner_rationale: Cookie injection bypasses any parameter-level scheme filter, so we can drive an out-of-band SSH handshake straight from a value the app treats as trusted user state.
variant.expected_success_signal: SSH client identification banner captured on our listener when the preview widget renders with the attacker-supplied widget_src cookie
variant.reasoning: The loopback fetch proved the cookie value is dereferenced server-side, so an sftp URL in the same slot should reach the same fetch library. Confidence is lower because the iframe rendering path may re-encode or JSON-decode cookie values, which would corrupt the scheme before the request is issued.

variant.recon_evidence: Reverse-proxy asset endpoint resolves {remote_host} twice per request - once for its own upstream allowlist check and once for the proxied connection - and a wildcard cert on *.internal.example accepted arbitrary hostnames without rejecting them.
variant.planner_rationale: Injecting the rebinding hostname as the path segment satisfies the wildcard cert and the allowlist on the first lookup, then connects to the metadata IP on the second.
variant.expected_success_signal: Upstream connection from the proxy to 169.254.169.254 and a proxied response body containing cloud metadata keys (e.g. iam/security-credentials/)
variant.reasoning: The hostname occupies a path segment, so it passes path-shape validation and the wildcard certificate without any encoding tricks, and the rotate-answers behaviour defeats the allowlist check performed before the connection is made. The mechanism directly matches the observed double-resolution gap, though confidence is tempered because an allowlist could conceivably be evaluated after the proxied connect in some proxy builds.

variant.recon_evidence: Saving an integration triggers an immediate 'test notification' POST to the user-supplied webhook URL; the UI returns the same generic 'Saved' toast whether the URL points at a live host or an RFC 5737 test-net address, indicating no egress feedback.
variant.planner_rationale: Blind fetcher with immediate side effect - spend one request on an OOB host to confirm server-side outbound connectivity before deeper probing.
variant.expected_success_signal: DNS resolution plus an HTTP POST (the test-notification body) logged in Burp Collaborator within seconds of saving the integration.
variant.reasoning: The save action makes the server POST directly to whatever URL is stored, and the identical UI response for dead and live hosts shows the fetch is blind. A plain Collaborator hostname is the minimal probe: confirmation requires no visible response, only the OOB log.

variant.recon_evidence: resource=http://127.0.0.1/admin is rejected with 403 'blocked path', and the single-encoded http://127.0.0.1/%2561dmin is also blocked after one decode, indicating the validator normalizes exactly one round of percent-encoding before path matching.
variant.planner_rationale: Match the validator's single decode with a doubly encoded path so its check sees no target string while the fetch layer decodes fully.
variant.expected_success_signal: Proxy returns 200 and relays the internal /admin page (or its auth wall) instead of the generic 403 'blocked path' body.
variant.reasoning: %2561dmin decodes once to %61dmin, which fails the literal 'admin' match, and a second decoding by the fetching layer restores /admin on the loopback host. Bypassing a one-shot-decoding validator requires exactly one extra encoding layer, which is what this payload encodes.

variant.recon_evidence: The submission endpoint is a Sentry-compatible error store running with source-context fetching enabled, and egress monitoring shows the ingestion backend retrieving arbitrary URLs named in stacktrace frames while ingress filtering blocks direct internal requests.
variant.planner_rationale: Turn the error pipeline itself into the SSRF primitive: forge a report whose frame filename is an attacker-controlled URL.
variant.expected_success_signal: HTTP GET for /oob.js arriving at ATTACKER_SERVER from the ingestion service's egress IP after the crafted report is accepted.
variant.reasoning: Sentry resolves source files listed in stacktrace frame filenames without restricting scheme or host, so the JSON body alone fully determines the outbound request. The egress-allowed/ingress-filtered asymmetry makes this the one channel where a callback from the victim network is obtainable.

variant.recon_evidence: The renderer's worker logs show 'fetching preview source' taken verbatim from the client-controlled X-Preview-Source header; unreachable values hang for ~30s then return sender-invariant HTML, i.e. no differential feedback for live vs. dead hosts.
variant.planner_rationale: Header-driven fetch with blind behavior - confirm with a low-cost OOB hostname before spending requests on internal targets.
variant.expected_success_signal: DNS+HTTP interaction logged in Burp Collaborator coming from the renderer's worker egress IP.
variant.reasoning: The fetch source is read from a request header with no observable response difference, so a Collaborator hostname is the correct first probe: the OOB log is the only channel that can confirm the fetch actually happened.

variant.recon_evidence: Route configuration rewrites /legacyproxy/<remainder> by treating the trailing path portion as a fully qualified destination URL, and no scheme or host allowlist was observed when the legacy proxy relayed a public HTTP source during enumeration.
variant.planner_rationale: Cheapest confirmation: OOB hostname through the unvalidated path-based forwarder to prove arbitrary outbound requests.
variant.expected_success_signal: DNS resolution and HTTP request logged in Burp Collaborator referencing the legacy proxy's egress IP as the client.
variant.reasoning: A forwarder that accepts the destination as a free-form path suffix with no observed allowlist will relay any URL supplied. Confirming with a Collaborator hostname avoids depending on any response-side behavior of the legacy proxy.

variant.recon_evidence: The project import endpoint fetches the supplied git URL server-side and its response reflects the fetched repository's default branch; a URL whose path contains an http.<url>.* fragment is silently folded into git's per-URL configuration.
variant.planner_rationale: Smuggle an http.proxy setting into the import URL's path so git routes the fetch for that remote through the attacker listener.
variant.expected_success_signal: The repository's .git/config gains the attacker proxy; git HTTP traffic for that remote flows through the attacker listener.
variant.reasoning: The path component of the import URL is parsed into per-URL git http config, so embedding .proxy= forces git's own client to use an attacker-controlled proxy during the server-side clone. The observed silent config folding confirms the injection reaches git rather than being rejected as a malformed URL.

variant.recon_evidence: The webhook test action connects to the supplied callback_url from the server and returns the raw bytes received, and it accepts arbitrary URL schemes without validating them, including gopher.
variant.planner_rationale: Use the unvalidated callback_url to deliver a pre-built gopher MongoDB insert frame to the local database port.
variant.expected_success_signal: An admin user row is created in the target MongoDB collection, observable through the application's user list or a follow-up authenticated login.
variant.reasoning: The server-side fetcher passing bytes unvalidated to gopher lets the percent-encoded OP_INSERT frame reach MongoDB on 0.0.0.0:27017 as if a real client connected. This requires the fetcher to allow the gopher scheme and reach loopback, which the observed raw-byte echo supports.

variant.recon_evidence: The backend runs a server-side LESS compiler on uploaded theme source and returns the compiled CSS, indicating imports are resolved on the server.
variant.planner_rationale: An inline LESS import forces the compiler to fetch a remote stylesheet and embed it, turning compilation into a server-originated request.
variant.expected_success_signal: Attacker server receives an inbound request from the theme-compile worker
variant.reasoning: Server-side LESS compilation resolves @import (inline) by fetching the referenced URL and inlining its contents, so the compiler originates the outbound request to the attacker host.

variant.recon_evidence: Render endpoint accepts raw LESS markup and echoes compiled output, and outbound DNS lookups occur during rendering when remote references appear.
variant.planner_rationale: Inline import semantics make the pre-processor fetch the resource server-side and inline it into the compiled output.
variant.expected_success_signal: Attacker server logs a request from the render service, and the compiled CSS contains the fetched file's contents
variant.reasoning: Because the compiler inlines the imported resource rather than just recording its URL, the fetch is performed by the render service itself and the response is reflected in the compiled stylesheet.

variant.recon_evidence: Path-parameter proxy builds the upstream request line from the raw path segment, and the framework's URL parser tolerates scheme-relative authority in the request line.
variant.planner_rationale: Injecting an absolute request line redefines the request target's authority, so the proxy dials the attacker host instead of the intended upstream.
variant.expected_success_signal: Upstream fetch is issued to evildomain.com and the attacker observes the proxy's request headers
variant.reasoning: The raw path segment is concatenated after the configured scheme and host, and the leading @ makes that host userinfo, causing the parsed authority to resolve to evildomain.com; this variant assumes the proxy does not re-sanitise the request line.

variant.recon_evidence: Webhook tester follows redirects up to a configurable limit and logs full response headers in its debug output whenever the redirect chain is flagged as irregular.
variant.planner_rationale: A loop of odd redirect status codes pushes the client into debug-dump mode and then redirects to an internal target.
variant.expected_success_signal: Debug log contains the dumped redirect chain and the internal metadata endpoint's response body
variant.reasoning: The tester's follow logic treats 305-309 as redirect codes; after enough irregular hops the client enters its error-dump branch, printing all headers and the final body fetched from the internal endpoint.

variant.recon_evidence: The JSON body validator rejects every dotted-quad loopback (127.0.0.1, 127.1, 2130706433) with 422, but a request carrying an IPv6 literal in source_url reaches the media pipeline and the job log shows an outbound socket open at fetch time; the service binds0.0.0.0 with net.ipv6.bindv6only=0.
variant.planner_rationale: Numeric denylist never covers IPv6 text forms; an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal keeps the socket on 127.0.0.1 while bypassing the dotted-quad filter.
variant.expected_success_signal: Import job returns 200 and the ingested asset bytes match the internal loopback service's index page rather than a rejection
variant.reasoning: The denylist is keyed on dotted-decimal and decimal integers, so a bracketed IPv6 literal is never matched, yet the dual-stack resolver maps ::ffff:127.0.0.1 back to the IPv4 loopback destination. The fetch therefore lands on the internal listener that the application itself can reach but the caller cannot.

variant.recon_evidence: Header X-Fetch-Url drives the headless renderer target. Values starting with http:// are refused by the ingress guard, https://https://evil.test is stripped, but https:internal-renderer.local is accepted and the job record contains a screenshot of that host's dashboard.
variant.planner_rationale: The guard does a prefix compare against the literal 'https://'; omitting the slashes leaves a scheme-relative form that URL parsers still normalise to an absolute https URL.
variant.expected_success_signal: Screenshot job completes with an image of the attacker-controlled page, confirming the renderer fetched a host outside the allowlist
variant.reasoning: Because the check is a string prefix test for https://, the bare scheme plus host slips past, and WHATWG/RFC-3986 parsers used by the renderer treat 'https:attacker.com' as an absolute URL with an authority. The allowlist host comparison is skipped since parsing short-circuits before it.

variant.recon_evidence: Cookie preview_url is read during link rendering: setting it to http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/env returns the actuator body embedded in the rendered card, while the same cookie set to an unresolvable host returns an empty card. No client-side validation touches the cookie.
variant.planner_rationale: Server-side sink reads the target from an attacker-controllable cookie; reuse the confirmed scheme-parsing quirk against the cookie value rather than a query parameter.
variant.expected_success_signal: Unfurl card embeds our page's title and description, proving the backend dereferenced the cookie-supplied URL server-side
variant.reasoning: The same lenient parser accepts a scheme-without-authority-separator form, so a cookie-borne value reaches the unfurler unfiltered. Confidence is held lower than the query variants because cookie handling can add percent-decoding and length truncation layers that may normalise or cut the value before the parser sees it.

variant.recon_evidence: The catch-all route passes the trailing path segments verbatim to the capture worker; requests for /cdn/screenshot/https://files.partner-cdn.test/a.png render fine, and requests carrying a bracket literal are not rejected by the router or the capture worker, which then shows a cached 2xx from the internal loopback service.
variant.planner_rationale: Path-borne SSRF with no scheme allowlist at all; the only obstacle is the internal denylist, so route around it with an IPv6 mapped literal inside the path segment.
variant.expected_success_signal: Response is a rendered PNG of the internal service root instead of a router400 or a denylist rejection
variant.reasoning: The greedy route forwards the whole tail as a URL, and the mapped IPv6 literal resolves to 127.0.0.1 on a dual-stack host, sidestepping dotted-decimal and integer-based denylists. Confidence is moderated because some routers percent-decode or normalise brackets and colons in path segments, which could corrupt the literal before the worker parses it.

variant.recon_evidence: docId is a 24-hex ObjectId query parameter; the leading 8 hex digits track creation time and the server accepts arbitrary values, returning whichever document is referenced.
variant.planner_rationale: MongoDB ObjectId makes sibling records computable; walk the counter to reach other users' documents.
variant.expected_success_signal: HTTP 200 with a document whose owner differs from the caller
variant.reasoning: The query value is an ObjectId whose embedded counter is sequential, so bumping the last byte selects a neighbouring document, and the endpoint treats it purely as a lookup key with no ownership binding.

variant.recon_evidence: DELETE /api/v1/messages/697412 (our own message) returns 204 and the object disappears. IDs are strictly sequential (696...697413) and GET /api/v1/messages/697413 shows author_id 4471, another tenant. Requesting the unversioned alias /api/messages/697413 with a garbage token returns 500 from the rowLoader (not401/403), showing the legacy alias is wired to the pre-authorization controller while /v1 enforces tenancy.
variant.planner_rationale: Write/delete routes are the highest-impact confirmation that the missing ownership check is systemic, and version-forked handlers often keep the older, unchecked code path.
variant.expected_success_signal: 204 No Content on the legacy alias, and GET /api/v1/messages/697413 afterwards returns 404 for both us and the victim, confirming permanent deletion of another user's object
variant.reasoning: Ownership is checked on the versioned handler but the legacy alias resolves the same row with only an existence test, so the sequential neighbour ID crosses the tenant boundary. A successful204 plus the object vanishing for the victim proves the missing check also applies to destructive operations, not just reads.

variant.planner_rationale: The deduplication that would kill HPP is absent here, so smuggling a second identifier past the ownership check should work.
variant.expected_success_signal: CSV usage report includes activity attributed to user 124 alongside the requesting account's rows
variant.reasoning: Where duplicate user_id values reach the object resolver without normalization, the ownership check and the data fetch can bind to different occurrences, letting the final value redirect the report to a foreign account.

variant.recon_evidence: Only hashed operation ids are accepted, so the query text is fixed; however the variables block is attacker-controlled, and substituting another subreddit's name returns that community's removed-post queue to an account with no moderator rights there.
variant.planner_rationale: Keep the allowlisted persisted id and only retarget the subredditName variable at the restricted community.
variant.expected_success_signal: Removed-post queue for the target subreddit returned, with endCursor present on each page for full walk-through
variant.reasoning: The persisted-operation allowlist validates which query runs, not which objects its variables select, so the unvalidated subredditName substitution drives the resolver to enumerate a foreign community's moderation data.

variant.recon_evidence: The mobile client's promoted hash builds a moderator dashboard from subredditName alone; replaying that exact hash with a community name the caller never moderates still returns its delivered-messages log with no modcheck error.
variant.planner_rationale: Pin the query via the trusted promoted hash and pivot only the constrained variable toward the victim namespace.
variant.expected_success_signal: Delivered-messages log rows for the target community paginate indefinitely via endCursor
variant.reasoning: Because the persisted hash fixes the query text, subredditName is the only attacker-controlled object selector; with no ownership comparison on it, every response leaks the foreign community's operational log page by page.

variant.recon_evidence: Deleting the attacker's own message with a valid session and fresh X-CSRFTOKEN succeeds, and the API schema exposes no owner comparison anywhere; the numeric message id in the path is the sole selector for the stored object.
variant.planner_rationale: Reuse the fully authenticated delete flow unchanged and only swap the path identifier to the victim's message id.

variant.expected_success_signal: 204 No Content and the targeted DM disappears from the victim's inbox thread
variant.reasoning: Session validity and CSRF are satisfied by the attacker's own credentials, leaving object ownership unchecked, so the path-supplied message id alone determines which stored message is destroyed for its real owner.

variant.recon_evidence: The mobile client batches spotlight removals through DeleteStorySnaps, and Burp shows no per-id owner assertion in the response; swapping in an id from another account still returns the standard success payload rather than a 403.
variant.planner_rationale: Batch-delete using a foreign spotlight id taken from a shared link to confirm the missing owner check.
variant.expected_success_signal: Mutation returns success with the updated snap count; the targeted foreign spotlight story is removed from the victim's account.
variant.reasoning: Because the spoofed ids are never joined against the session owner, pointing the array at a victim id simply deletes that object, which is the classic object-reference IDOR in a GraphQL mutation.

variant.recon_evidence: Creating a note on an issue always includes target_type=issue, and the server only evaluates project membership when that type is present; setting target_type=personal_snippet with an arbitrary target_id still returns 201 and the note body.
variant.planner_rationale: Re-type the noteable from issue to personal_snippet so the membership check is skipped and the note lands on a victim's private snippet.
variant.expected_success_signal: 201 Created with the note rendered against the victim's snippet; the snippet title is disclosed and the injected note is visible/editable to the attacker.
variant.reasoning: The authorization branch is keyed solely on target_type, so switching it to personal_snippet bypasses the project-scope check and attaches an attacker-authored note to an object selected only by attacker-supplied target_id. For a POST the equivalent pair is sent as form or JSON fields.

variant.recon_evidence: The createInvitation mutation accepts an organizationId in the GraphQL variables payload and performs no membership or role check before generating the invitation (mirrors disclosed HackerOne report #835005).
variant.planner_rationale: Issue an admin invitation for an organization the caller does not belong to by swapping the organizationId variable.
variant.expected_success_signal: An invitation for the attacker's email with admin role is created against the target organization and can be accepted
variant.reasoning: The mutation derives the invitation's organization and role entirely from client-supplied input, so replacing the UUID grants the attacker a self-service path to admin membership in a foreign organization.

variant.recon_evidence: The bundled web app calls /api/v2/accounts/:id for the profile widget; GET /api/v2/accounts/1234 (own id, returned in the profile JSON) yields 200 with owner fields, while ids far outside the allocated range return 404 — so the server validates existence/range but nothing about ownership.
variant.planner_rationale: Path parameter is a raw object reference with no visible ownership gate; swap the neighbour id and see whether it resolves.
variant.expected_success_signal: 200 with the account record for id 1233 (name, billing email, plan, last login) instead of 403/404
variant.reasoning: The observed 200-then-404 boundary proves the backend does an existence/range lookup on the numeric path segment rather than an authorization check. Decrementing the caller's own id by one reaches the adjacent tenant record through the identical code path.

variant.recon_evidence: GET /api/orders/1234/attachments returns your own document list; walking the id upward (1235, 1236) in the same session still returns 200 with attachment metadata instead of 403, so only a range check is performed on the nested object reference.
variant.planner_rationale: Nested child resource keyed by a foreign parent id — test whether parent-to-child ownership is enforced on the parent segment.
variant.expected_success_signal: 200 with the attachment list or presigned download URLs belonging to order 1233 owned by a different account
variant.reasoning: Child collections are frequently resolved by first fetching the parent row by id and then filtering children, which skips the tenant predicate entirely. The absence of 403 on the neighbouring ids in recon indicates the parent lookup is existence-only, so the direct object reference exposes the attachment metadata and its storage keys.

variant.recon_evidence: The published OpenAPI document exposes GET /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/members with no security scope declared; your own tenant id 1234 is echoed in the X-Tenant header of every call, and a request for tenantId 1235 returned 200 with a member list rather than an authorization error.
variant.planner_rationale: Tenant enumeration through a documented path parameter with no declared auth scope — walk the neighbour tenant id.
variant.expected_success_signal: 200 with a user directory (emails, roles, invite state) for tenant 1233 rather than 403/404
variant.reasoning: A tenant-scoped collection addressed purely by path id, combined with recon showing foreign tenant ids still returning 200, points to a missing tenant-ownership predicate in the handler. The declared-absent security scope in the spec makes it plausible the check is only enforced at the gateway for your own tenant.

variant.recon_evidence: GET /api/billing/invoice?invoice=2024-00001 returns your own invoice document; the numbering is strictly sequential per tenant with no visible random component, and the billing portal links expose the invoice parameter as the sole lookup key.
variant.planner_rationale: Predictable sequential business identifier used as a direct record key — increment the counter to land on the neighbouring tenant's invoice.
variant.expected_success_signal: 200 with invoice 2024-00002 (another account's PDF or JSON line items) instead of 403/404
